title: Carrier Point Destination
description: A parcel locker or staffed pickup point operated by a carrier network, not by the Business. The point is identified by the tuple (`network`, `country`, `point_id`); the Business-scoped `id` is used for selection.

type.description: Destination type discriminator. Optional in requests under a `carrier_pickup` method, where it defaults to `carrier_point`.

id.description: Destination identifier used by `selected_destination_id`. In requests, a Platform-chosen ID for a point it writes; in responses, the ID the Business recognizes for this point within the method.

network.description: Carrier network whose rules and point directory apply, as a reverse-domain name derived from a domain the network operator controls (e.g. `com.example-parcel`). A network that keeps separate point namespaces under different brands uses a distinct value per namespace. This is the operating network, not a broker or the host where the point sits.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code of the point. Part of the point key: networks operate in several countries and do not guarantee point IDs unique across them. Never inferred from `point_id`.

point_id.description: Point identifier as issued by `network`, unique within (`network`, `country`). Opaque: compared as an exact, case-sensitive string, leading zeros preserved, never parsed.

broker.description: Aggregator or broker through which the point was selected, when its point identifier differs from the network's own `point_id`. Lets the Business re-resolve the point through the same integration.

point_id.description: The broker's own identifier for the same point. Opaque.

point_type.description: Kind of point. Well-known values: `locker` (automated parcel locker, collected with a code), `staffed` (counter at a host or network branch, handed over by staff). Businesses MAY use additional values.

name.description: Buyer-facing name of the point, as the network or Business presents it.

address.description: Postal address of the point. It is the point's address, not the Buyer's.

host.description: Physical site that houses the point, such as a shop or a fuel station. One site can host points of several networks; each is a separate destination with its own `network`, `point_id` and terms.

id.description: Business-scoped identifier of the site, equal across the destinations located at the same site. Opaque.

pickup_period.description: How long the network holds a parcel at this point after deposit, as advertised before purchase. The binding deadline for a parcel is the `pickup_by` timestamp on its deposit event.

counting.description: How days in `duration` are counted. Well-known values: `calendar_days`, `business_days`. Absent means calendar time.

limits.description: Parcel limits of this point, for display. Eligibility is decided by the Business and reported through `available` and `unavailable_reasons`.

max_dimensions.description: Maximum parcel dimensions, largest first. A parcel fits when each of its dimensions, also sorted largest first, is at most the dimension at the same position.

available.description: Whether the Business can currently deliver the method's line items to this point. Absent means available.

unavailable_reasons.description: Machine-readable reasons why the point cannot be used. Present only when `available` is `false`.

code.description: Reason code. Well-known values: `exceeds_size_limit`, `exceeds_weight_limit`, `item_not_eligible` (an item the network does not accept at points, independent of size), `point_full`, `point_closed` (temporarily out of service), `point_not_found` (unknown to or removed from the network directory), `network_not_supported`, `country_not_supported`. Businesses MAY use additional values.

line_item_ids.description: Line items that cause this reason, when it is item-specific.
